title: Slow Cooker Tomato, Cabbage & Bean Soup
description: Cabbage, white beans, tomatoes, and potatoes simmer into an inexpensive hands-off soup made from ordinary groceries.
substitutions: Use kidney beans or chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use sweet potato instead of regular potato.
Add a handful of frozen vegetables during the final 30 minutes if desired.

steps.text: Put everything in the slow cooker.
Cook until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 4 cups chopped cabbage, 2 cups diced potatoes, 1 drained can white beans, 1 can diced tomatoes, 4 cups broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Taste, adjust seasoning if needed, and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Broccoli, Potatoes & White Beans
description: Crisp-edged potatoes, broccoli, and white beans roast together for a simple meatless sheet-pan dinner.

ingredients.item: white beans, drained, rinsed, and patted dry

substitutions: Use cauliflower or green beans instead of broccoli.
Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Sprinkle with Parmesan after roasting if desired.

steps.text: Add broccoli and beans and finish roasting.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 1/2 pounds cubed potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and half the pepper. Spread on a large sheet pan.
Add 4 cups broccoli and 1 drained can white beans. Toss with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and remaining pepper.
Roast for 15 more minutes, until the broccoli is browned at the edges and the potatoes are tender.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a hot oven or skillet for best texture.

title: Leftover Pasta, Tomato & Egg Skillet
description: Cold leftover pasta gets a second life with tomatoes, eggs, and cheese in a fast skillet meal.
substitutions: Use a few spoonfuls of jarred pasta sauce instead of diced tomatoes.
Use any melting cheese you have.
Add leftover cooked vegetables if available.

steps.text: Warm and lightly crisp the leftover pasta.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon oil or butter in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add 2 cups cold leftover pasta and cook for 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until hot and lightly crisp at the edges.
Add 1/2 cup diced tomatoes and 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning. Cook 1 minute. Beat 2 eggs, pour them into the skillet, and stir gently for 2–3 minutes until just set.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup shredded cheese and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper. Cover for 1–2 minutes until the cheese melts, then serve.

storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat until hot.

title: Small-Batch Applesauce Oat Muffins
description: A half-dozen soft cinnamon muffins turn applesauce and pantry oats into an easy small-batch breakfast or snack.
substitutions: Use quick oats instead of old-fashioned oats.
Use white sugar if brown sugar is unavailable.
Fold in 1/4 cup raisins or diced apple if desired.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease 6 muffin cups. In a bowl, mix 3/4 cup flour, 1/2 cup oats, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Stir in 1/2 cup applesauce, 1 egg, and 2 tablespoons melted butter or oil just until no dry flour remains. Divide among the 6 muffin cups.
Bake for 18 minutes, until the tops spring back lightly and a toothpick comes out without wet batter.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days. Freeze up to 2 months.
